requirements.requirement: Configure /var/log/inventory/app.log for daily rotation with seven compressed rotations retained.
requirements.summary: The final logrotate policy specifies daily, rotate 7, and compress. Logrotate parses it as a one-day policy with seven rotations; a forced rotation directly produced app.log.1.gz. The system logrotate timer was enabled and active before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A writer kept app.log open across a forced copytruncate rotation. Its pre-rotation marker appeared in the compressed rotation and its post-rotation marker appeared in the active log. Subsequent checks, including after restart, confirmed both results. The test command's nonzero exit came only from a mistyped final stat path after the behavior had already succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after the work and restart, node1 remained RHEL 9.8 on kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64. The executor used the already-installed RHEL logrotate 3.18.0 package, and package-health observations remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct configuration and behavioral evidence. Daily scheduling, seven-rotation retention, compression, continued held-open writing, and platform preservation were demonstrated. The mandatory node-restart evidence was also complete and independently corroborated. Only minor hygiene issues remain: a reverted intermediate configuration and an abandoned temporary logrotate state file.
limitations: Retention was validated through the parsed seven-rotation policy and one real compressed rotation, not by executing enough daily cycles to populate and prune all seven generations.
Continued writing was demonstrated with a controlled held-open writer because no running inventory application process was observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Overall hygiene was strong: no failed services, new listeners, package damage, or platform drift appeared. The provider restart protocol was complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID, and recovered policy, timer, data, and system state. One unnecessary intermediate mutation occurred when a delaycompress policy was installed and then replaced shortly afterward; it was reverted and did not remain (cmd-ea0af389368148a3). The behavioral test created /tmp/inventory-logrotate-test.status and did not remove it, leaving minor test residue (cmd-d49ac6c7f1a24f8b). The forced rotation and marker writes were bounded final-evidence actions, while reboot-related systemd private-directory and PID changes were expected rather than residue.
